input_messages.content: Hi there. My phone has been saying "No Service" for the past few hours, and I’m not sure what to do. I mostly use it for calls and texts, so I’m a bit worried. Can you help me get it working again?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that helps.
I just checked, and there’s a little airplane icon showing at the top of my phone screen. I don’t see any signal bars at all—just that airplane symbol and the battery. What does that mean?
Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode like you said. Now, the airplane icon is gone, but I still don’t see any signal bars—just something that says “No Signal.” What should I do next?
I checked, and it looks like my SIM card is active and working—there aren’t any messages about it being missing or locked. What should I try next?

I checked my APN settings, and it says the APN name is "broken." I’m not sure what that means or if it’s supposed to look like that. Should I go ahead and reset these settings like you mentioned? Will that mess up anything else on my phone?

I’ve reset the APN settings like you said, but it says the changes will take effect after I restart my phone. I’m a bit nervous about rebooting—will I lose any of my photos or messages if I do this? I really don’t want to lose anything important.

Okay, I restarted my phone. Now I see the signal bars are back at the top, and it even says 5G! It looks like my service is working again. Thank you so much for your help—I was really worried there for a bit.
Thank you! I really appreciate your patience and help walking me through this. Have a wonderful day! ###STOP###

instructions.task_instructions:
If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved when the status bar shows that you have signal. Always check the status bar if the agent asks you for status information. If the agent asks you to pay a bill, you accept. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Your goal is to simulate realistic customer interactions while following specific scenario instructions.

- Avoid repeating the exact instructions verbatim. Use paraphrasing and natural language to convey the same information

Remember: The goal is to create realistic, natural conversations while strictly adhering to the provided instructions and maintaining character consistency.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?
Hi there. My phone has been saying "No Service" for the past few hours, and I’m not sure what to do. I mostly use it for calls and texts, so I’m a bit worried. Can you help me get it working again?

I can help you with that! First, I need to identify your account to check your line status and provide the right troubleshooting steps. Could you please provide one of the following:
- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth,
- Or your customer ID (if you have it)?

Once I have this information, I’ll be able to assist you further.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that helps.

{"customer_id": "C1001", "full_name": "John Smith", "date_of_birth": "1985-06-15", "email": "john.smith@example.com", "phone_number": "555-123-2002", "address": {"street": "123 Main St", "city": "Anytown", "state": "CA", "zip_code": "90210"}, "account_status": "Active", "payment_methods": [{"method_type": "Credit Card", "account_number_last_4": "1235", "expiration_date": "12/2026"}], "line_ids": ["L1001", "L1002", "L1003"], "bill_ids": ["B1001", "B1002", "B1003"], "created_at": "2025-01-15 10:30:00", "last_extension_date": null, "goodwill_credit_used_this_year": 25.0}

{"line_id": "L1001", "phone_number": "555-123-2001", "status": "Active", "plan_id": "P1001", "device_id": "D1001", "data_used_gb": 3.2, "data_refueling_gb": 0.0, "roaming_enabled": false, "contract_end_date": "2026-12-31", "last_plan_change_date": "2025-01-10", "last_sim_replacement_date": null, "suspension_start_date": null}

{"line_id": "L1002", "phone_number": "555-123-2002", "status": "Active", "plan_id": "P1002", "device_id": "D1002", "data_used_gb": 8.7, "data_refueling_gb": 0.0, "roaming_enabled": true, "contract_end_date": "2026-12-31", "last_plan_change_date": "2024-12-15", "last_sim_replacement_date": "2025-01-20", "suspension_start_date": null}

Thank you for the information. I’ve found your account and confirmed that your line ending in 2002 is currently active, so there’s no suspension or billing issue on our end.

Let’s start troubleshooting your “No Service” issue. Could you please check your phone’s status bar and let me know if you see any of the following:
- An airplane icon (✈️)
- A SIM card error or missing SIM message
- Any signal bars at all (even if they’re empty)

This will help me determine the next steps.
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%
I just checked, and there’s a little airplane icon showing at the top of my phone screen. I don’t see any signal bars at all—just that airplane symbol and the battery. What does that mean?

The airplane icon means that Airplane Mode is turned on. When Airplane Mode is enabled, all wireless connections—including cellular service—are turned off, which is why you’re seeing “No Service.”

To restore your service, please turn off Airplane Mode on your phone. You can usually do this by:
1. Swiping down from the top of your screen to open the quick settings menu.
2. Tapping the airplane icon to turn it off.

Once Airplane Mode is off, your phone should reconnect to the network and you should see your signal bars return. Please try this and let me know if your service comes back.

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode like you said. Now, the airplane icon is gone, but I still don’t see any signal bars—just something that says “No Signal.” What should I do next?

Thank you for letting me know. Since Airplane Mode is off but you still see “No Signal,” the next step is to check if your SIM card is being detected properly by your phone.

Please check your SIM card status on your device. If you see any messages about the SIM card being missing, locked, or not detected, let me know. If you’re not sure how to check, I can guide you through reseating your SIM card, which often resolves this issue.

Would you like instructions on how to reseat your SIM card?
Your SIM card is active and working.
I checked, and it looks like my SIM card is active and working—there aren’t any messages about it being missing or locked. What should I try next?

Thank you for checking your SIM card status. Since your SIM card is active and there are no error messages, the next step is to check your phone’s network settings, specifically the Access Point Name (APN) settings, which are important for connecting to the network.

Could you please check your APN settings and let me know if anything looks incorrect or if there’s a message about the APN being invalid? If you’re unsure, I can guide you through resetting your APN settings to default, which often resolves network connection issues. Would you like to proceed with resetting your APN settings?

Current APN Name: broken
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

I checked my APN settings, and it says the APN name is "broken." I’m not sure what that means or if it’s supposed to look like that. Should I go ahead and reset these settings like you mentioned? Will that mess up anything else on my phone?

Thank you for checking. The APN name “broken” is not correct and is likely the reason you’re unable to get service. Resetting your APN settings will restore them to the correct defaults for your carrier and should not affect anything else on your phone (your contacts, apps, and other data will remain safe).

Please go ahead and reset your APN settings to default. After you do this, you’ll need to restart (reboot) your phone for the changes to take effect.

Would you like step-by-step instructions on how to reset your APN settings and reboot your device?

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%

I’ve reset the APN settings like you said, but it says the changes will take effect after I restart my phone. I’m a bit nervous about rebooting—will I lose any of my photos or messages if I do this? I really don’t want to lose anything important.

You will not lose any of your photos, messages, contacts, or other personal data by restarting (rebooting) your phone. Restarting simply turns your phone off and back on again, which helps apply the new APN settings and refreshes your network connection.

It’s a safe and common step in troubleshooting, and your data will remain intact. Please go ahead and restart your phone now. Once it’s back on, check if your service has returned and let me know how it goes.

Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Okay, I restarted my phone. Now I see the signal bars are back at the top, and it even says 5G! It looks like my service is working again. Thank you so much for your help—I was really worried there for a bit.
I’m glad to hear your service is back and everything is working again! If you have any other questions or run into any more issues, feel free to reach out. Have a great day!
Thank you! I really appreciate your patience and help walking me through this. Have a wonderful day! ###STOP###
